The Invisible Victims of Identity Theft: Our Kids

Part of the problem is that the social security number was not designed to be a form of authentication. It's a form of identification that found widespread use in government and industry mainly because the Social Security Administration was the first government agency to automatically enroll every american citizen.

Prior to the SSA, you would only engage with a government agency if you were related through military service (Dept of Veteran's Affairs) or a vocation that required federal licensing / certification, or if you registered a patent, etc. SSA was applied to everyone (even the Census Bureau didn't track individuals with any sort of ID number), so the SSA was only federal agency with a "complete set" of ID numbers on American's born after a certain year.

Thus, the SSN became a de-facto identifier for all things government and financial. "Identity theft" is a consequence of our lack of true formal authentication methods. If I know all the personal identifying information for an individual, that does not prove that I am that individual. Banks do not seem to understand this.
Combine that with the ease of getting people's details via social media and unsecured networks, and you've got yourself and epidemic.
